THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
S.G.PANDIT, J., MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The claimant/injured is before this Court in this appeal filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, questioning the correctness and legality of the Judgment and award dated 21.06.2019 in MVC No.281/2016 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM and Addl.
MACT, Dharwad, by which the claim petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is dismissed on the ground that the appellant has failed to prove the accident

. 
2. Heard learned counsel Sri. Prashant S. Kadadevar, appearing for the appellant and learned counsel Smt. Preeti Shashank, appearing for the respondent No.2.
Perused the appeal papers as well the tribunal records.

3. The brief facts of the case are that, the appellant/claimant filed claim petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident occurred on 09.01.2016 when the claimant was proceeding as a pillion rider on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-24/U-456.
It is stated that, the claimant/appellant was working as a driver and earning Rs.15,000/- per month and was aged 22 years at the time of accident.
4. On service of notice, both the respondents appeared before the tribunal and filed their objections.
The respondent No.1 in his objection denied the claim petition averments and also categorically denied the factum of accident.
It is also contended that the rider of the motorcycle was not having valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
The Insurer in its objection statement stated that, the claim petition is filed suppressing the material facts.
Learned counsel further stated that, on the date of accident, the claimant himself was riding the motorcycle and it was a case of self fall.
It is also contended that, there is a delay of two days in lodging the complaint and it is stated that, his father was not riding the motorcycle.

sentences.text: Having regard to the contentions of the parties, the tribunal framed issued as to whether the claimant/petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries pointing out the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle and held the issue in the negative.
6. The claimant himself examined as P.W.1 apart from marking documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
The respondent marked documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.7, apart from examining R.W.1.
The tribunal on scrutiny of the materials on record, under the impugned Judgment and award dismissed the claim petition with compensatory cost.

7. Learned counsel Sri. Prashant S. Kadadevar, appearing for the appellant, strenuously contends that the finding of the tribunal that the claimant has not proved the accident is contrary to the material on record.

Further learned counsel inviting attention of this Court to Ex.P.6 the wound certificate and Ex.P.7 the charge-sheet, would submit that the claimant sustained injuries in a road traffic accident, and Ex.P.6 - wound certificate is the earliest document in which the reason for injury is recorded and the same shall have to be believed.

Further, learned counsel would submit that, the charge-sheet is to be read as whole and if it is read as whole, it is clear that the claimant/injured has sustained injuries in a road traffic accident and it is not a self fall as contended by the insurer.
8. Learned counsel would further submit that, the accident had taken place on 09.01.2016 and the complaint was filed on 11.01.2016 by the claimant himself.
It is submitted that, though the motorcycle was ridden by the father of the claimant he could not lodge the complaint, since he had also suffered minor injuries.
9. Learned counsel would further submit that, the accident had taken place on 09.01.2016 at about 9.15 p.m. and his cousin Sri. Sultansab had brought the claimant in 108 Ambulance to the hospital.

Thus, he prays for allowing the claim petition and to award compensation for the injuries sustained by the claimant/appellant.
10.

Per contra, learned counsel Smt. Preeti Shashank submits that, the tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim petition as the claimant sustained injuries as a self fall from the bike and it is not a road traffic accident.
Learned counsel would also submit that, it is the case of the claimant that the father of the claimant was riding the motorcycle and the claimant/appellant was a pillion rider.

If the accident had taken place on 09.01.2016 and if the claimant had suffered grievous injuries, the father who has sustained minor injuries could have lodged the complaint, but the complaint is not lodged by the father, but the claimant himself has filed the complaint after two days.
Learned counsel would further refer to the MLC i.e. Ex.R.2 would submit that, the MLC is the earliest document which records that the claimant has sustained injury as a self fall.
Learned counsel would also point out that the wound certificate is dated 19.02.2016 which is subsequent to all other documents, moreover, a month subsequent to other documents.

Learned counsel would also submit that, the discharge summary indicates that when the claimant/appellant was admitted to the hospital there was no history of unconsciousness and therefore, it is submitted that, the claimant could have lodged the complaint immediately or the next day.

Even otherwise, she submits that the father who was riding the bike had suffered minor injuries, could have lodged the complaint Dilawar S/O Rafiqsab Kotwal vs Noorahemad S/O Divansab Toragal on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116733070/
3 immediately.

sentences.text: 11. Learned counsel would also submitted that, the charge-sheet is filed against the rider of the bike i.e. the father who pleaded guilty which itself would be sufficient to hold that it is a case of implicating the motorcycle to claim compensation.
Thus, she prays for dismissal of the appeal.

12. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers as well as the Trial Court records, the only point which falls for our consideration is as to, Whether the appellant has made out a case for interfering with the impugned judgment and award?

Our answer to the above point would be in the Negative for the following reasons:
13.
The alleged accident is said to have taken place on 09.01.2016 while the claimant was proceeding as pillion rider along with his father on the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-24/U-456.
The Wound Certificate as well as MLC would indicate that the accident has taken place on 09.01.2016 at about 09.10 p.m., and 08.00 p.m., respectively.

The Wound Certificate which is dated 19.02.2016/22.02.2016 records cause of injury as RTA, whereas the MLC which is dated 09.01.2016 and immediately forwarded to the police authorities by the hospital indicates history of injury as "self fall" from bike.
14. With the above factual background, it is to be examined as to whether the claimant has sustained injuries in a road traffic accident by examining the attending circumstances.
Admittedly, it is the case of the claimant/appellant that claimant was proceeding as a pillion rider along with his father.
According to the claimant himself, his father has sustained minor injuries.
The father of the claimant has not lodged complaint.
The claimant himself lodges complaint after two days i.e., on 11.01.2016.
There is no reason forthcoming as to why the father failed to lodge complaint as on the date of accident or on the next day.
It is also to be seen that when the claimant was admitted to hospital, there was no history of unconscious.
The claimant himself has given history.

When there was no history of unconsciousness, loss of consciousness or bleeding, the complainant could have himself lodged complaint or could have instructed his father to lodge complaint immediately.
Moreover, charge sheet is filed against the father of the claimant and the father of the - 10 - claimant pleaded guilty.
All these circumstances would give rise to suspicion with regard to the accident and as to whether the claimant has suffered injury in a road traffic accident.
The Tribunal has recorded a finding that in the cross-examination of the claimant-PW1 that when he was confronted with Ex.R4, has answered evasively.
There is no cogent material to accept the contentions of the appellant that the claimant/appellant sustained injuries in a road traffic accident.
There is no merit in the appeal and accordingly appeal stands rejected.
